title: The jathedar

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Akal Takht's role: gurmatas on principle, hukamnamas for Sikhs everywhere. Your line was one voice for the panth.

A voice needs a mouth. Yesterday the Akal Takht spoke for the panth, but a building can't read a letter aloud, sign it, or stand on the steps while the sangat listens. Somebody does that. In news from Punjab the title turns up just before a name: Jathedar. It can sound like a rank in an army, or the head of a church. It isn't quite either. The word has a smaller, everyday meaning too, and that meaning still sits inside the title.
screen: `A VOICE NEEDS A MOUTH.` → `A TITLE BEFORE A NAME.` → `JATHEDAR.`

segments.voice: Start with the smaller word. A jatha is a band of Sikhs moving together for a purpose: a group of volunteers, a company of riders, a party of marchers, a kirtan group traveling from town to town. The jathedar is the one who leads the jatha. This path has met that use already, in the bands of the Khalsa's hard years and the jathas of the gurdwara reform movement, walking out together, unarmed, toward the shrines. Now the larger use. Each of the Takhts has a jathedar, the person who heads it. The Jathedar of the Akal Takht is the one people hear about, because edicts for the whole panth go out from there. A jathedar presides over the Takht's business, reads out its hukamnamas, and can summon Sikhs to answer before it. So: a leader of a moving band, and the head of a seat that doesn't move. Some readers hear the first inside the second: the jathedar of a Takht still leads a jatha, only now the band is the whole panth, and the job is to keep it moving together. Then a caution, so the title isn't misheard. A jathedar is not a pope and not a Guru. Sikhs say the Guru is the Granth and the Panth, which this path met a few days ago. The jathedar serves the Takht; the Takht doesn't belong to the jathedar. How jathedars are appointed is a live question among Sikhs, argued in good faith. But whoever holds the seat holds the same task.
screen: `JATHA: A BAND MOVING TOGETHER.` · `EACH TAKHT HAS A JATHEDAR.` · `THE BAND BECOMES THE WHOLE PANTH.` · `A SERVANT OF THE TAKHT, NOT A GURU.` · then, large: `THE LEADER OF THE TAKHT.`

segments.voice: Think of the best leader of a small band you've ever been part of, a coach, a shift manager, an older cousin on a road trip, and find one thing they did that kept everyone moving together. Maybe they walked at the pace of the slowest, or spoke last; hold that one thing, and breathe.
Jathedar. The leader of a jatha, a band of Sikhs, and the title of the person who heads each of the Takhts. Today's word.
